goal: The runner's record exclusion matches declared record files exactly and record directories at a path boundary, so source files that share a record's prefix stay visible
brief:
Write the regression tests for contract A. (1) New file test_record_paths.py at the project root: unittest TestCase classes runnable as `python3 -m unittest test_record_paths.py`, every method named with its sentence id (test_R1_... to test_R7_...). (2) test_hacheong.py's test_the_tree_checks_leave_out_the_records_the_lock_declares asserts the bare "hunsu" in record_paths()'s tuple — that expectation codifies the defect: amend exactly those two record_paths() expectations to R1's tuples, deliberately, and change nothing else in test_hacheong.py. Import the candidate from this directory (`import worker`), never an installed plugin. Fixtures are temporary git repositories (tempfile), removed afterwards; no model, host or network calls — validators are called directly (worker.validate with a member from worker.load_member, as test_hacheong.py does) with an empty or synthetic transcript. Every test must fail today, if it fails, by an assertion (assertX / self.fail), never by an import, attribute, loader or runtime error: probe anything the build must add through assertions, and keep fixtures correct. Run both files once: test_record_paths.py must show failures only (zero errors) from the R1-R5 defect, and `python3 test_hacheong.py` must show the amended test as FAIL with AssertionError and every other test PASS. R6-R7 are preservation sentences whose tests may pass now and after the build. Do not change test_native_prompt.py, test_hostcall_env.py or any non-test file.

CONTRACT A (sentences R1-R7). Defect: worker.record_paths() always adds a bare "hunsu" and tree_state() leaves out every path that startswith() any record entry, so source files hunsu.py, hunsu_helper.py and hunsu-notes.md are hidden as if they were environment records, and a declared record file hides its prefix neighbours (e.g. declared "hunsu.json" hides "hunsu.json.bak"). The refactor inventory, meanwhile, skips record directories wherever they appear in the tree and never skips an exact record file. Fix: one exact-file versus directory-boundary rule, applied by every consumer of record_paths(). No traversal redesign, no import of any sibling plugin's module.

ENV = the five hunsu environment files, exactly: hunsu.json, hunsu.lock.json, hunsu-judgments.json, hunsu-conflicts.md, hunsu.local.json.

R1. record_paths(target) returns a sorted tuple of unique strings: ".chongdae/" and the five ENV files always; plus every path the lock's `record-paths` mapping declares (the union of its values) — or, when hunsu.lock.json has no `record-paths` mapping (no lock, unreadable JSON, or `record-paths` not a dict), the fallback ".mangsang/", ".dwitbuk/", "reviews/". It never contains a bare "hunsu" or any other entry. Exactly: with no lock -> (".chongdae/", ".dwitbuk/", ".mangsang/", "hunsu-conflicts.md", "hunsu-judgments.json", "hunsu.json", "hunsu.local.json", "hunsu.lock.json", "reviews/"); with a lock {"record-paths": {"alpha": [".alpha/"], "beta": []}} -> (".alpha/", ".chongdae/", "hunsu-conflicts.md", "hunsu-judgments.json", "hunsu.json", "hunsu.local.json", "hunsu.lock.json").
R2. The rule. Paths are relative to the project root, with "/" separators, and record entries are anchored at that root. An entry ending in "/" is a directory record: it covers every path under it, at any depth (declared "reviews/" covers "reviews/a.json" and "reviews/x/y.json"), and never a sibling that merely shares its prefix ("reviews-old/a.json", "reviewsx/a.py", "reviews.md") nor a same-named directory deeper in the tree ("docs/reviews/a.json", "app/reviews/models.py"); a nested declared directory follows the same boundary (declared "docs/rec/" covers "docs/rec/x.json", not "docs/record/x.json" nor "docs/rec.md"). An entry without a trailing "/" is a file record: it covers exactly that one path — never a prefix neighbour ("hunsu.json.bak", "hunsu.jsonx", "notes.rec.bak", "notes.recx" next to declared "notes.rec") nor the same name deeper in the tree ("sub/hunsu.json").
R3. tree_state(target) leaves out exactly the paths R2 says are records (besides what it already leaves out: __pycache__ paths, .pyc and .DS_Store). So hunsu.py, hunsu_helper.py, hunsu-notes.md, prefix neighbours of declared files and directories, and same-named paths deeper in the tree appear in its state when created or changed, while the five ENV files, anything under ".chongdae/" and every declared record stay out.
R4. inventory(target, at_head) leaves out the same records by the same rule, for at_head=True (git HEAD) and at_head=False (the working tree) alike — directory records and exact file records both: a declared exact Python record file (e.g. "gen_record.py", or ".tool/gen_record.py" inside a dot-directory) is counted in neither, while its neighbour "gen_record_tool.py", hunsu.py, hunsu_helper.py and "app/reviews/models.py" (a same-named directory deeper in the tree than a declared "reviews/") are counted in both. Its existing non-record skips stay as they are (".git/", "__pycache__/", ".venv/", "tests/", "test/" wherever they appear). Parity: for a committed tree with no uncommitted changes, inventory(target, True) == inventory(target, False), with records, record neighbours and dot-directories present.
R5. The validators see what R3 shows. A member whose policy has no-tree-changes (e.g. sibi) and whose call changed hunsu.py, hunsu_helper.py or hunsu-notes.md is failed (status "failed", "no-tree-changes" in validation.failed); a member with only-tests-touched (e.g. teujip) whose call changed hunsu_helper.py outside the tests it declared is failed with the non-claim "only-tests-touched: changed outside the tests it declared: hunsu_helper.py" (no transcript, or one that names the file). A call that changed only an ENV file (e.g. hunsu.lock.json or hunsu-conflicts.md) or a file under ".chongdae/" or a declared record directory fails neither validator.
R6. Protected tests keep their protection (preservation): tests-kept still compares each requested test's contents from before and after the call, so a build that changes a requested test is refused even when the test sits at a record path (e.g. under ".chongdae/" or a declared record directory) or is committed.
R7. Nothing else changes (preservation): worker.py imports nothing from a sibling plugin; red-before-build, checks-ran, quotes-required and explanation-kept behave as before apart from seeing the newly visible paths; test_native_prompt.py and test_hostcall_env.py keep passing.
